rubric_notes: Concise but complete: core histones (a.22.1.1), archaeal (a.22.1.2), TAF/CHRAC/NC2/NF-Y/Sos (a.22.1.3), bacterial Aq_328/TTHA1479 (a.22.1.4) in superfamily a.22.1 (47113) in SCOPe 2.08; superfamily supports probable common ancestry while separate families mark divergence and do not justify transferring nucleosome assembly, DNA packaging, or transcriptional function; fold and class explicitly insufficient for homology; H1/H5 (a.4.5.13), H-NS (a.155.1.1), and histone-modifying enzymes correctly excluded; template caveats appropriate. Identifiers supported by bundle. Evaluator: claude-fable-5-1; 2026-10-22.

Correct families a.204.1.2 and a.204.1.4, shared superfamily a.204.1 and fold a.204 in SCOPe 2.08; remote homology as probable common origin rather than fold similarity; family divergence noted; rejects bidirectional transfer of HisE/MazG function, substrate specificity, mechanism, pathway role, and states superfamily membership alone is insufficient. All claims bundle-supported. No must_avoid violations. Evaluator: claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-22.

Correct families, SUNIDs, superfamily, fold and class, supported including superfamily children listing. Superfamily not fold as basis for homology, conserved actin-like structural/nucleotide-coupling framework, rejects transfer of substrate, reaction, regulation, oligomeric state, cellular role, architecture; appropriate template caveat. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 judge; 2026-10-22. Correct families, superfamily a.25.1 and fold a.25 with SUNIDs matching bundle (sccs parents endpoints). States shared superfamily supports probable remote common ancestry rather than analogous folding, with family split marking divergence; refuses to transfer ferroxidase, radical/cofactor or peroxide-disproportionation chemistry, active-site geometry, metal identity, oligomeric assembly; requires family-specific profile and catalytic-residue conservation, metal-site structural comparison, cofactor and activity assays. Concise but hits all required elements with no errors.

Correct class/fold/superfamily/family placements with SUNIDs, supported by bundle. States superfamily membership implies probable remote homology while families remain separate. Cites family comments that ephrin and PAD4 N-terminal domains lack the metal-binding site; refuses transfer of copper binding/electron transfer and requires conserved ligand geometry, metal-binding/spectroscopic measurements and redox assays. Distinguishes core-fold template from copper-site/functional template. No errors.

Correct identifiers for all three families, superfamily d.15.1, fold d.15; supported by bundle. Frames superfamily as remote evolutionary relationship, describes family-specific functional divergence, and explicitly forbids transferring covalent-modifier/E1-E2-E3 roles, p97/Cdc48 binding, and Ras binding across families; requires family-specific sequence and biochemical evidence. Complete. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct families c.23.1.1/c.23.1.4/c.23.1.5 with SUNIDs 52173/52252/82344 under CheY-like superfamily c.23.1, fold c.23, release 2.08; all supported by bundle. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Evaluator claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-22. Correct classification of all three superfamilies and fold with bundle-supported SUNIDs; correctly refuses merger and function/template transfer. Evidence list (sequence, phylogenetic, structure-based) omits motif and biological-context evidence, and the answer never states that separation does not establish nonhomology. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct three-family/one-superfamily placement with correct SUNIDs; superfamily interpreted as remote common ancestry stronger than fold resemblance; unsafe transfer of ADH catalysis, CoA binding, NAD binding, channel regulation explicitly rejected; domain vs whole-protein caveat (RCK regulatory domain not pore; c.2.1.1 only the C-terminal domain). N-terminal all-beta comment supported by bundle annotations. Required external evidence listed. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

States shared class k, fold k.40, superfamily k.40.1, and nominal family k.40.1.1 with family SUNID 100905 annotated 'not a true family' (in bundle); concludes placement does not establish evolutionary homology and supports only structural/design similarity as designed trimeric coiled-coils; rejects function transfer and template inference without independent evidence. States d1a14h2 (SUNID 343393, H:1-8, SCCS l.1.1.1) is a synthetic N-terminal tag in the Artifacts class, distinguishes it from the biological Ig heavy-chain variable domain d1a14h1, and rejects tag similarity for homology, family/superfamily assignment, function transfer, and template selection, recommending masking. All claims supported by the parents/sid bundle. Concise but complete; d1a14h1 boundary is given by the prompt. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1); 2026-10-22.

States shared family a.298.1.1 with full lineage (superfamily a.298.1, fold a.298, class a), attributes the 51/373/752-residue spread to differing tandem-repeat copy number, cites the 'single repeat' comment, the 're' repeat-number heterogeneity on d2kq5a_ and d3v6pa_, and the canonical representative repeat 4cj9 A:259-292 with the correct caveat that those coordinates are not boundaries for the other domains. Declines transfer of repeat count, DNA-target specificity, and whole-chain templating. All cited values match its evidence bundle. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 judge; timestamp 2026-10-22.

Correct examples: c.2, c.3, c.31, d.58.20, e.52 NAD-kinase-like; correct c.2.1 families (c.2.1.1 ADH-like, c.2.1.2 tyrosine-dependent oxidoreductases, c.2.1.3 GAPDH-like, c.2.1.4 formate/glycerate DH NAD-domain). Treats cross-fold similarity as convergent 'or at least lacking demonstrated common ancestry', an appropriate caveat. Divergence placed at superfamily/family level with correct relative strength; neither level guarantees function. Explains chemical-constraint convergence and lists domain-wide evidence (sequence with coverage, topology, boundaries, structural alignment beyond pocket, phylogeny) plus biochemical evidence for function transfer; template guidance sound. All criteria met. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

Concise but complete: 2.04 ColG b.23.2.1 in CUB-like fold versus Cry3A b.18.1.3 (residues 500-644) in galactose-binding-domain-like, sharing only the all-beta class, which is explicitly stated not to imply homology; 2.08 ColG reassigned to b.18.1.36 giving shared superfamily b.18.1 but a still-distinct family. Supporting evidence spans conserved beta-sandwich core plus the 1nqjA representative FATCAT hit to the same-family Cry4Ba domain d1w99a3 (p=0.00395, RMSD 2.52, 2.5% identity), correctly flagged as family-level sampling rather than a direct 1nqd-1dlc superposition, with the 99.16% 1nqdA-to-1nqjA mapping stated accurately. Function used as compatible support only, with explicit refusal to transfer collagen binding, calcium dependence, collagenase activity, or Cry receptor specificity, and template use limited to the shared core.

Evaluator claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-22. Correctly keeps homology at family (and shared Engrailed protein/species) level, states hf does not negate it, gives hf semantics (different fold despite similar sequence and SS count), rejects template, geometry, binding-specificity and function transfer, and requires independent alignment, structural comparison, construct and quality checks; says training sets should preserve the hf caveat and not treat the pair as same-fold replicates. Release 2.08, family/superfamily, and mutant/NHE annotations are supported by the bundle. Concise but complete; no material omission or error.

Strongest evidence: cites SEQRES (99) vs ATOM (50) residue counts for d1o5dt2 and 104/104 for d1uc6a1, all matching the sequence endpoints in its bundle, giving a concrete basis for the fr annotation. Family homology retained but functions not interchangeable; alignment uses genetic sequence with coordinate-missing positions masked and structure comparison on mutually resolved regions; d1uc6a1 preferred as whole-domain representative with quality considered separately (1o5d 2.05 A X-ray vs 1uc6 NMR effective 4 A, both correct); d1o5dt2 retained as local observation; diversity from complete structures only; cR9 interface and function transfer rejected. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

Correctly recommends a new superfamily in the existing fold; states that a new family asserts probable ancestry plus a closer relationship; new fold requires distinct architecture/topology and is not justified merely by unproven homology; notes separation does not prove non-homology and that later sequence-profile, structural, or mechanistic evidence could revise placement (hypothesis framing). Avoids all must_avoid items and rejects fold-only function transfer. The a.4 / a.4.5 / a.4.5.54 hierarchy illustration is supported by the evidence bundle. Evaluator: claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-22.

Names class d, fold d.144, superfamily d.144.1 and the three families d.144.1.4, d.144.1.6, d.144.1.7 in SCOPe 2.08 (supported by bundle children/parents/homology). Clearly separates class/fold similarity (architecture only) from superfamily (remote common ancestry of the catalytic domain) and limits the claim to the domain, not full proteins or orthology. Mechanistic inference (bilobal scaffold, NTP donor, metal, phosphoryl transfer) is appropriate; divergence of acceptor surfaces across the three families is stated, and substrate, phosphorylation position, inhibitor sensitivity, kinetics and physiological role are explicitly not transferable. Evidence requirements include family-level sequence relationship, conserved catalytic/substrate-contacting residues, ligand-bound structural comparison, substrate panels, kinetics, mutagenesis, cellular/genetic evidence, and full-length regulatory context. SUNIDs not given but not required. Evaluator: claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-22.
